Statement 3 is correct: The chapter on the Union Judiciary (Articles 124 to 147) comes immediately before the chapter on the Comptroller and Auditor-General. Statement 4 is incorrect: that chapter (Article 213) belongs to Part VI; Part V has the Legislative Powers of the President (Article 123).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Parts in which certain Articles lie:

1. Article 72, on the President's power to grant pardons, lies in Part V (The Union Government).
2. Article 161, on the Governor's power to grant pardons, lies in Part V (The Union Government).
3. Article 163 lies in the chapter on the Legislative Powers of the Governor.
4. Article 123 lies in the chapter on Parliament (Articles 79 to 122).

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 72, on the President's power to grant pardons, lies in Part V (The Union Government). Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 161 lies in Part VI (Articles 152 to 237). Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 163 lies in Chapter II (The Executive, Articles 153 to 167); the chapter on the Legislative Powers of Governor consists of Article 213 alone. Statement 4 is incorrect: Article 123 forms a separate chapter, the Legislative Powers of the President. So exactly 1 correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 is correct (statement 1).
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 is correct (statement 1).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 1 is correct (statement 1).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Parts in which certain Articles lie, as shown by Tables 4.1 and 4.2:

1. Article 16, on equality of opportunity in public employment, lies in Part III (Fundamental Rights).
2. Article 46, on the educational and economic interests of scheduled castes, scheduled tribes and other weaker sections, lies in Part III (Fundamental Rights).
3. Article 45, on early childhood care and education, lies in Part IV (Directive Principles).
4. Article 30, on the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions, lies in Part IV (Directive Principles).

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 16, on equality of opportunity in public employment, lies in Part III (Fundamental Rights). Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 46 lies in Part IV (Directive Principles, Articles 36 to 51). Statement 3 is correct: Article 45, on early childhood care and education, lies in Part IV (Directive Principles). Statement 4 is incorrect: Article 30 lies in Part III (Articles 12 to 35). So exactly 2 correct.
w: 'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 3).
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 3).
'None' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 3).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about single-Article units of the Constitution:

1. Part VII, before its deletion, consisted of a single Article, 238.
2. The chapter titled General in Part VI consists of a single Article, 152.
3. The chapter on Subordinate Courts in Part VI consists of a single Article.
4. The chapter on the Legislative Powers of the Governor in Part VI consists of a single Article, 213.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Part VII, before its deletion, consisted of a single Article, 238. Statement 2 is correct: The chapter titled General in Part VI consists of a single Article, 152. Statement 3 is incorrect: it covers Articles 233 to 237. Statement 4 is correct: The chapter on the Legislative Powers of the Governor in Part VI consists of a single Article, 213. So exactly 3 correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 4).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 4).
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 4).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Part IX-A and Part IX-B did not form part of the Constitution as originally enacted.
Statement-II: Part IX-A (The Municipalities) was added by the 74th Amendment Act (1992) and Part IX-B (The Co-operative Societies) by the 97th Amendment Act (2011).

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: both Parts were inserted later by amendment. Statement-II is correct: Part IX-A (Municipalities) was added by the 74th Amendment Act (1992) and Part IX-B (Co-operative Societies) by the 97th Amendment Act (2011). Having been inserted by later amendments is exactly why neither was in the Constitution as originally enacted.
w: Option 'both correct, II does not explain I' is rejected: II does explain I, because insertion by the 74th and 97th Amendments is why the Parts were not original.
Option 'I correct, II incorrect' is rejected: Statement-II is correct: the Note ongives the 74th (1992) and 97th (2011) Amendments.
Option 'I incorrect, II correct' is rejected: Statement-I is correct: both Parts were added by amendments.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Fundamental Duties are placed in Part IV-A, between Part IV (Directive Principles) and Part V (The Union Government).
Statement-II: The Fundamental Duties form a part of the Directive Principles in Part IV of the Constitution.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: Part IV-A (Article 51-A) comes after Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) and before Part V, and consists of only one Article. Statement-II is incorrect: the duties have a Part of their own, Part IV-A; Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) holds the Directive Principles.
w: Option 'both correct, II explains I' is rejected: Statement-II is incorrect, because the duties are not in Part IV but in the separate Part IV-A.
Option 'both correct, II does not explain I' is rejected: Statement-II is incorrect for the same reason: Part IV-A is separate from Part IV.
Option 'I incorrect, II correct' is rejected: Statement-I is correct: Part IV-A sits between Part IV and Part V.

o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect

questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the Fundamental Duties were borrowed from the Soviet Constitution. Statement-II is correct: the ideal of justice (social, economic and political) in the Preamble was also borrowed from it. They are two separate borrowings from the same source; borrowing the justice ideal gives no reason for borrowing the duties.
w: Option 'both correct, II explains I' is rejected: the justice ideal and the Fundamental Duties are separate borrowings, so II gives no reason for I.

Option 'I incorrect, II correct' is rejected: Statement-I is correct: the Fundamental Duties were borrowed from the Soviet Constitution.
